For the thinking behind these pages, see [How I teach](philosophy.qmd).

Most of my teaching material started out as Jupyter notebooks: exercises for
the *Theoretical Neuroscience* lecture at Goethe University Frankfurt, and a
webinar I gave for the German Neuroscience Olympiad in 2020. Notebooks are
great for a course, but they are a hassle to open just to look at one plot.
So I have moved the parts that benefit most from playing around onto these
pages, where they run directly in the browser.

Each page has one small simulation and a handful of sliders. The simulation
keeps running while you move a slider, so you can watch what a parameter does
rather than read about it. The text is meant to make sense on its own, but it
is not a replacement for the book. The exercises come from Dayan and Abbott's
*Theoretical Neuroscience*, and the format is borrowed from Dirk Brockmann's
[Complexity Explorables](https://www.complexity-explorables.org/).
